items.stem: What is the difference between equity and equality?
options: Equity means equal incomes; equality means fair incomes
Equity refers to wealth; equality refers to income
Equity means fairness; equality means everyone has the same
items.answer: Equity means fairness; equality means everyone has the same
items.markingKey: Equity is a normative concept about fairness; equality is equal shares.

items.stem: Explain the difference between horizontal equity and vertical equity.
items.answer: Horizontal equity: people in the same circumstances are treated the same. Vertical equity: people in different circumstances are treated differently, e.g. the rich pay more tax.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each [2]

items.stem: Explain why an equal distribution of income may not be equitable.
items.answer: People differ in needs, effort, skills and responsibilities; giving everyone the same income ignores these differences and may reduce incentives.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: different needs/effort; 1 mark: incentives [2]

items.stem: Chloe has $20,000 in a savings account. Is this an example of income or wealth?
items.answer: Wealth
items.markingKey: Wealth: a stock of financial assets.

items.stem: Yusuf owns shares in Delta Foods worth $50,000. Is this an example of income or wealth? Explain your answer.
items.answer: Wealth: a stock of assets at a point in time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Wealth; 1 mark: explanation – a stock of assets at a point in time. [2]

items.stem: Extract: Income inequality in Korvia has risen; the Gini coefficient increased from 0.28 to 0.34. The government plans to raise the minimum wage by 5%, introduce a higher top rate of income tax and replace universal child benefit with a means-tested benefit. Business groups warn of job losses and reduced incentives. (a) Calculate the percentage increase in the Gini coefficient. (b) Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of switching to a means-tested child benefit.
items.answer: (a) 21.4% (b) Targets help, lower cost vs low take-up, stigma, admin cost, poverty trap.
items.markingKey: (a) (0.34 − 0.28)/0.28 × 100 [2] (b) Credit: Targets help, lower cost vs low take-up, stigma, admin cost, poverty trap. [2]

items.stem: What is the difference between income and wealth?
options: Income is a flow of money over time; wealth is a stock of assets at a point in time
Income is a stock; wealth is a flow
Wealth is earned from work only
items.answer: Income is a flow of money over time; wealth is a stock of assets at a point in time
items.markingKey: Flow vs stock.

items.stem: Explain how wealth can generate income.
items.answer: Assets earn returns: property earns rent, savings earn interest, shares pay dividends; so wealthy people receive extra income.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: assets yield returns; 1 mark: example [2]

items.stem: In Fendaria, the richest 10% of households receive 35% of income but own 60% of wealth. Explain why wealth is more unequally distributed than income.
items.answer: Wealth accumulates over generations through inheritance and returns on assets; those with high incomes can save more, adding to wealth, while poorer households save little.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: inheritance/accumulation; 1 mark: saving and returns [2]

items.stem: Chloe makes the following statement: ‘Equity means that everyone should have exactly the same income.’ Explain why this statement is incorrect.
items.answer: Equity means fairness; equality means the same shares. A fair distribution may still be unequal.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – Equity means fairness; equality means the same shares. A fair distribution may still be unequal. [2]

items.stem: Total household income in Esteria is $100 billion and there are 5 million households. Quintile (20% of households): Poorest, Second, Third, Fourth, Richest; Share of income (%): 6, 11, 16, 22, 45. Calculate how many times greater the income share of the richest 20% is than that of the poorest 20%.
Classify each as income or wealth and explain. (i) Mohammed owns shares in Silverline worth $50,000. (ii) Mohammed receives a state pension each month.
items.answer: (i) Wealth (ii) Income
items.markingKey: (i) Wealth – a stock of assets at a point in time. [2] (ii) Income – a transfer payment received over time. [2] Total [4]

items.stem: Mateo, an economics student in Kuala Lumpur, is preparing for a class debate on this topic. Explain the difference between income and wealth and between equity and equality.
items.answer: Income = flow; wealth = stock; sources of each; equity normative fairness (horizontal/vertical); equality same shares.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: Income = flow; wealth = stock; sources of each; equity normative fairness (horizontal/vertical); equality same shares. items.stem: What is a progressive tax?
options: A tax that takes a smaller proportion from the rich
A tax on goods and services
A tax where everyone pays the same amount
A tax where the proportion of income paid in tax rises as income rises
items.answer: A tax where the proportion of income paid in tax rises as income rises
items.markingKey: Average rate rises with income.

items.stem: Explain how a progressive income tax combined with transfer payments can reduce income inequality.
items.answer: Higher earners pay a larger proportion of income in tax, reducing top incomes; the revenue funds transfers to low-income households, raising their incomes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: progressive tax reduces high incomes; 1 mark: transfers raise low incomes [2]

items.stem: Explain two possible disadvantages of a national minimum wage.
items.answer: Unemployment if set above equilibrium; higher costs for firms and prices; may not target the poorest households (many are not in work); informal employment.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each, 1 mark each explained [4]

items.stem: Income tax bands in Dravonia are: 0–$10,000: 10%; $10,000–$60,000: 20%; above $60,000: 40%. Calculate the tax paid on an income of $36,000.

Income tax bands in Loristan are: 0–$10,000: 0%; $10,000–$60,000: 20%; above $60,000: 40%. (a) Calculate the tax paid and the average tax rate for incomes of $25,000 and $100,000. (b) State the marginal tax rate for each person. (c) Explain whether the tax is progressive.
items.answer: (a) $25,000: tax $3,000, average 12%; $100,000: tax $26,000, average 26%. (b) 20% and 40%. (c) Progressive: the average rate rises with income.
items.markingKey: (a) tax for each [2]; average rates [1] (b) marginal rates [1] (c) rising average rate → progressive [1] [5]

items.stem: Explain the difference between the average rate and the marginal rate of income tax.
items.answer: Average rate = total tax ÷ total income; marginal rate = tax on an extra unit of income. In a progressive system the marginal rate is above the average rate.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each definition [2]

items.stem: The government of Lunaria raises the top rate of income tax from 40% to 50%. Explain one possible benefit and one possible problem.
items.answer: Benefit: more revenue for redistribution, lower inequality. Problem: reduced incentives to work/invest, tax avoidance or emigration of high earners.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: benefit; 1 mark: problem [2]

items.stem: Jovania raises its minimum wage by 10%. Explain why the effect on employment depends on the elasticity of demand for labour.
items.answer: If demand for labour is inelastic, few jobs are lost; if elastic, firms cut employment significantly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: inelastic small effect; 1 mark: elastic large effect [2]

items.stem: Income tax bands in Lunaria are: 0–$15,000: 0%; $15,000–$60,000: 20%; above $60,000: 40%. Calculate the tax paid on an income of $30,000.

Income tax bands in Jovania are: 0–$12,000: 0%; $12,000–$60,000: 25%; above $60,000: 45%. (a) Calculate the tax paid and the average tax rate for incomes of $36,000 and $80,000. (b) State the marginal tax rate for each person. (c) Explain whether the tax is progressive.
items.answer: (a) $36,000: tax $6,000, average 16.7%; $80,000: tax $21,000, average 26.2%. (b) 25% and 45%. (c) Progressive: the average rate rises with income.

items.answer: Progressive income tax: average rate rises with income; transfers: benefits and pensions to low-income groups; redistribution; examples.

items.stem: What is a means-tested benefit?
options: A benefit paid only to workers
A benefit paid to everyone in a group
A benefit paid only to those whose income or wealth is below a certain level
items.answer: A benefit paid only to those whose income or wealth is below a certain level
items.markingKey: Targeted at those in need.

items.stem: What is a universal benefit?
options: A benefit paid only to the poorest
A benefit paid to everyone in a group regardless of income
A benefit paid only to the unemployed
items.answer: A benefit paid to everyone in a group regardless of income
items.markingKey: e.g. child benefit for all families.

items.stem: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of universal benefits compared with means-tested benefits.
items.answer: Advantage: high take-up, no stigma, cheap to administer, no poverty trap. Disadvantage: expensive, part goes to the better-off.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: advantage; 1 mark: disadvantage [2]

items.markingKey: After tax 180.0; benefit withdrawn 50% of that; keep 90.

items.stem: In Ostrelia, a worker on benefits earns an extra $100 a week. Income tax of 20% is paid on the extra earnings, and the means-tested benefit is withdrawn at 70 cents for each dollar of after-tax earnings. (a) Calculate the amount the worker keeps and the effective marginal tax rate. (b) Explain how this illustrates the poverty trap and suggest one policy to reduce it.
items.answer: (a) Keeps $24; effective marginal rate 76%. (b) High combined withdrawal of benefits and tax means little gain from working more, discouraging work; reduce the taper rate, raise tax-free allowance, or use in-work benefits.

items.stem: Mei, an economics student in Santiago, is preparing for a class debate on this topic. (a) Explain how progressive taxation and transfer payments can be used to reduce inequality. (b) Assess whether a national minimum wage is the most effective way to reduce poverty in Korvia.
items.answer: (a) Progressive income tax: average rate rises with income; transfers: benefits and pensions to low-income groups; redistribution; examples. (b) For: Raises pay of lowest earners; no direct cost to government; reduces in-work poverty. Income tax bands in Rovania are: 0–$12,000: 0%; $12,000–$50,000: 25%; above $50,000: 45%. (a) Calculate the tax paid and the average tax rate for incomes of $36,000 and $80,000. (b) State the marginal tax rate for each person. (c) Explain whether the tax is progressive.
items.answer: (a) $36,000: tax $6,000, average 16.7%; $80,000: tax $23,000, average 28.8%. (b) 25% and 45%. (c) Progressive: the average rate rises with income.
items.markingKey: (a) tax for each [2]; average rates [1] (b) marginal rates [1] (c) rising average rate → progressive [1] [5]

items.stem: Lina, an economics student in Karachi, is preparing for a class debate on this topic. (a) Explain how progressive taxation and transfer payments can be used to reduce inequality. (b) ‘A national minimum wage is the most effective way to reduce poverty in Esteria.’ Discuss this statement.
items.answer: (a) Progressive income tax: average rate rises with income; transfers: benefits and pensions to low-income groups; redistribution; examples. (b) For: Raises pay of lowest earners; no direct cost to government; reduces in-work poverty. Against: Job losses, informal sector, does not help non-workers; transfers and education may be more effective; depends on level set and labour market. Conclusion: a reasoned judgement on when the claim holds.
items.markingKey: (a) Indicative content: Progressive income tax: average rate rises with income; transfers: benefits and pensions to low-income groups; redistribution; examples. Level 3 (6–8): accurate knowledge with a clear, developed analytical chain and, where relevant, an accurate, labelled diagram that is used in the answer; Level 2 (3–5): some correct explanation but undeveloped or partly inaccurate; Level 1 (1–2): limited knowledge, mostly assertion [8] (b) Analysis (AO1/AO2, up to 8): Raises pay of lowest earners; no direct cost to government; reduces in-work poverty. Evaluation (AO3, up to 4): Job losses, informal sector, does not help non-workers; transfers and education may be more effective; depends on level set and labour market. Top marks need balanced analysis of both sides and a justified conclusion that answers the question set, explaining what the outcome depends on [12]

items.stem: What is the poverty trap?
options: A situation where prices rise faster than wages
A situation where everyone receives benefits
A situation where earning more leaves a person little better off because benefits are withdrawn and taxes rise
items.answer: A situation where earning more leaves a person little better off because benefits are withdrawn and taxes rise
items.markingKey: High effective marginal tax rate.

items.stem: In a revision note Daniel wrote: ‘Means-tested benefits are always better because they only go to the poor.’ Identify what is wrong with this reasoning and give the correct explanation.
items.answer: They cost less, but take-up is often low, they are costly to administer and can create a poverty trap.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: identifies the error; 1 mark: correct explanation – They cost less, but take-up is often low, they are costly to administer and can create a poverty trap. [2]

items.stem: In Calvania, a worker on benefits earns an extra $100 a week. Income tax of 20% is paid on the extra earnings, and the means-tested benefit is withdrawn at 80 cents for each dollar of after-tax earnings. How much of the extra $100 does the worker keep?
items.markingKey: After tax 80.0; benefit withdrawn 80% of that; keep 16.

items.stem: Extract: Income inequality in Valdoria has risen; the Gini coefficient increased from 0.35 to 0.41. The government plans to raise the minimum wage by 10%, introduce a higher top rate of income tax and replace universal child benefit with a means-tested benefit. Business groups warn of job losses and reduced incentives. (a) Explain the difference between equality and equity. (b) Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of switching to a means-tested child benefit.
items.answer: (a) Equality = same shares; equity = fairness, a normative concept. (b) Targets help, lower cost vs low take-up, stigma, admin cost, poverty trap.
items.markingKey: (a) Credit: Equality = same shares; equity = fairness, a normative concept. [2] (b) Credit: Targets help, lower cost vs low take-up, stigma, admin cost, poverty trap. [2]
